title: yadgar/gateway
description: EVERY KEY THIS CHART DECLARES, AND A REFUSAL FOR EVERYTHING ELSE UNDER THEM (ADR-0850). `chart/values.yaml`'s own blocks are declared one by one below, so an adopter's typo under any of them — `autoscalng`, `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespac`, `toolsPoll.intervalSecond` — is a REFUSAL NAMING THE KEY rather than a value merged into a document nothing reads it from. Helm enforces it in both `helm lint` and `helm template`, which is the `helm lint and render` pre-commit hook and therefore `ci / passed`, and it is also what an Argo sync meets.
$comment:
CLOSURE IS PER CHART (ADR-0850): this file closes only the keys gateway's OWN `values.yaml` and templates read, and says nothing about any other chart's keys — the parent and the platform chart each own their own closure, and a sibling module chart's schema is a separate file entirely.

THREE PATHS STAY OPEN, deliberately. `global` is Helm's own reserved key, shared with every subchart (ADR-0722) — this chart reads it only through `_hostname.tpl`'s `.context.Values.global`, and what else lives under it belongs to the parent and the other subcharts, not to this file. `resources` is a raw `corev1.ResourceRequirements` this chart re-types nowhere (`templates/deployment.yaml`). `rollingUpdate` is a raw `appsv1.RollingUpdateDeployment`, read the same way (`with .Values.rollingUpdate` in `templates/deployment.yaml`).

TWO EXTRAS ARE DECLARED AS LEAVES because `values.yaml` never states them. `image.digest` is read by `templates/deployment.yaml`; the CI release workflow rewrites it into a published chart at package time and no tag (D65, D61), so `values.yaml` ships no default for it. `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` is read by `templates/networkpolicy.yaml`; declaring it here is why `scrapeFrom` itself is a CLOSED block rather than an open map.

TYPES, TOGGLE SHAPES AND `required` LIVE IN `render-checks.yaml` (ADR-0847), NOT HERE: a block written as a scalar PASSES this schema and reaches the render check's own named refusal instead — measured, `autoscaling: "x"` passes this file and is `templates/render-checks.yaml`'s `must be a map` sentence. The exceptions predate this file and stay unchanged: `networkPolicy` and `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom` carry `type: object`, `networkPolicy.enabled` is `type: boolean`, `networkPolicy.clients` is `type: array` with typed-object items, `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` is `type: string`, and `toolsPoll` is `type: object` with `intervalSeconds` `integer, minimum 1`. A non-bool `networkPolicy.enabled` is therefore a schema refusal, not a render-check sentence. `networkPolicy.clients`' items keep their typed-object shape for the same reason stated on that block: this chart's `from` peers are not another module's workload-name list, and a value nothing here re-types is a value the API server, not this schema, would refuse at apply.

enabled.description: Whether to render the policy at all. False by default on asymmetric cost: a wrong policy on an enforcing CNI is an outage, and an absent one is no worse than today.

clients.description: The `from` peers admitted to the serving port, written as the NetworkPolicy API writes them. Empty while `enabled` is true is REFUSED by the template rather than rendered, because an empty or missing `from` matches ALL sources (ADR-0664).

items.description: One NetworkPolicyPeer. Selectors written in ONE entry are an AND; the same two written as two entries are an OR and admit far more.

namespace.description: The one namespace admitted to the metrics port. The metrics port serves without authentication, so ADR-0770 scopes it by namespace rather than leaving it open to the cluster.

scrapeFrom.description: Where the metrics scrape comes from. Absent renders no rule for the metrics port at all.

networkPolicy.description: The ingress allow-list rendered by chart/templates/networkpolicy.yaml. DECLARED HERE BECAUSE THIS CHART'S `clients` IS TYPED DIFFERENTLY FROM ITS SIBLINGS': every other module chart takes a list of workload NAMES and renders `podSelector: {app: <name>}` for each, while this one takes `from` PEERS, because the pods that dial this module's serving port carry `app.kubernetes.io/name` rather than `app` and run in their own namespace. A list of names pasted from a sibling chart is valid YAML that helm renders happily and only the API server rejects — a silent failure until apply. Typing the items as objects converts it into a refusal naming this key, at render time.

toolsPoll.description: Overrides for chart/config/gateway.yaml's `toolsPoll` section — read only by `gateway`, which is the only service that builds the `tools/list` response.

intervalSeconds.description: How often, in whole seconds, `gateway` tells an MCP client to re-poll `tools/list` for a changed tool catalogue. `0` is refused here rather than read as `off`: `rotate::GatewayDocument::tools_poll_interval` returns `ToolsPollError::Zero` for it, so a zero that passed the render would only fail later, at boot.
